subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2024 General Knowledge - Set A Q42 (Option B)
question_text:
With reference to Money Bills and Financial Bills in the Parliament of India, consider the following statements:
1. Every Money Bill is a Financial Bill, but not every Financial Bill is a Money Bill.
2. A Financial Bill (I) containing matters under Article 110 can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President.
3. The Rajya Sabha has no power to amend or reject a Financial Bill (II) that involves expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
explanation: Statement 1 is correct: All Money Bills (Article 110) are Financial Bills (Article 117), but only those containing exclusively Article 110 matters certified by the Speaker are Money Bills. Statement 2 is correct: Financial Bill (I) under Article 117(1) can be introduced only in Lok Sabha with President recommendation. Statement 3 is incorrect: Financial Bill (II) under Article 117(3) is treated like an ordinary bill in all respects, meaning Rajya Sabha has equal powers to amend or reject it.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity (7th Ed.), Chapter 22 Parliament: Financial Bills.
elimination_trap: Aspirants often confuse Financial Bill (II) with Money Bills. Rajya Sabha has equal powers over Financial Bill (II).

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Statement 2 is also valid under Art 117(1).
option_analysis.B: Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are constitutional facts under Arts 110 & 117(1).
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false as RS has full powers over Financial Bill (II).
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Statement 3 fails.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2024 Paper I - Set B Q18 (Option C)
question_text: In the context of the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution of India, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: The Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
The Governor is empowered to organize and re-organize the autonomous districts.
Acts of Parliament automatically apply to Autonomous Districts unless specifically excluded by the Governor.
Each autonomous district has a district council consisting of not more than 30 members.
explanation: Option C is NOT correct: Under Paragraph 12/12A of the Sixth Schedule, Acts of Parliament do NOT automatically apply to Autonomous Districts in Meghalaya, Mizoram, etc., unless the Governor or President specifically directs with or without modifications. Options A, B, and D are verbatim provisions of the Sixth Schedule.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 42 Scheduled and Tribal Areas.
elimination_trap: Extreme word "automatically" should raise immediate suspicion; the Sixth Schedule provides a protective legislative shield for tribal self-governance.

option_analysis.A: Correct statement (AMTM states).
option_analysis.B: Correct statement under Paragraph 1(3).
option_analysis.C: Incorrect statement (hence correct answer): Application requires presidential/gubernatorial notification.
option_analysis.D: Correct statement: 26 elected + 4 nominated members.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2023 General Knowledge - Set C Q65 (Option C)
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the writ of Quo-Warranto in India:
1. It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of the claim of a person to a public office.
2. It prevents illegal usurpation of a public office by a person.
3. Unlike other writs, it can be sought by any interested person, even if not an aggrieved person.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
1 and 3 only
explanation: All three statements are correct: Quo-Warranto literally means "by what authority". It is issued to prevent illegal usurpation of a substantive public office of a permanent character created by statute or constitution. The principle of locus standi is relaxed for Quo-Warranto, meaning any citizen or interested person can approach the court.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 7 Fundamental Rights: Writs.
elimination_trap: Candidates often think locus standi is strictly required for all writs, but Quo-Warranto and Habeas Corpus have relaxed rules.

option_analysis.A: Incomplete: Statement 3 is well settled in Supreme Court jurisprudence.
option_analysis.B: Incomplete: Statement 1 is the core definition.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are all accurate.
option_analysis.D: Incomplete.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2023 Paper I - Set A Q29 (Option A)
question_text: Which of the following statements regarding a Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament in India is correct?
options: In the absence of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Deputy Speaker presides over the Joint Sitting.
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides if the Speaker is absent.
A Joint Sitting can be summoned for Constitutional Amendment Bills in case of deadlock.
A Joint Sitting is governed by the Rules of Procedure of the Rajya Sabha.
explanation: Option A is correct: Under Article 118(4), if the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker presides. If Deputy Speaker is also absent, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha presides. Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice President) NEVER presides as he is not a member of either House. Joint Sitting cannot be summoned for Money Bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills, and it is governed by Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 22 Parliament: Joint Sitting.
elimination_trap: Common trap: Assuming Vice President (Chairman RS) presides. Vice President cannot preside over Joint Sitting.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha is 2nd in line of succession.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Chairman RS is explicitly barred.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Joint Sitting is strictly prohibited for Constitution Amendment Bills (Art 368).
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Governed by Rules of Lok Sabha.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2023 General Knowledge - Set D Q81 (Option C)
question_text:
Under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution of India, a nominated member of a House becomes disqualified for being a member if he/she joins any political party:
(a) Within six months from the date of taking seat
(b) At any time during the entire tenure
(c) After six months from the date of taking seat
(d) Only if declared by the Election Commission
options: Within six months from the date of taking seat
At any time during the entire tenure
After six months from the date of taking seat
Only if declared by the Election Commission
explanation: Option C is correct: Under paragraph 2(3) of the Tenth Schedule, a nominated member can join a political party within 6 months of taking his seat without disqualification. If he joins after the expiry of 6 months, he stands disqualified. (Note: Independent members are disqualified if they join ANY political party at any time).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 80 Anti-Defection Law.
elimination_trap: Candidates mix up nominated members (who have a 6-month window) with independent members (who have zero window).

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Within 6 months they are legally permitted to join.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: That rule applies to independent members, not nominated.
option_analysis.C: Correct: After expiry of 6 months triggers disqualification.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Disqualification is decided by the Speaker/Chairman, not EC.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2022 General Knowledge - Set A Q15 (Option B)
question_text: During the proclamation of a National Emergency under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution, the enforcement of which of the following Fundamental Rights CANNOT be suspended by the President under Article 359?
options: Articles 14 and 19
Articles 20 and 21
Articles 19 and 21
Articles 21 and 22
explanation: Option B is correct: By the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978, the right to move the court for the enforcement of the Fundamental Rights guaranteed by Articles 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offences) and 21 (protection of life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended under Article 359 even during a National Emergency.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 16 Emergency Provisions.
elimination_trap: Article 19 is automatically suspended under Article 358 during war/external aggression, but Articles 20 and 21 remain inviolable.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Article 19 can be suspended.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Articles 20 and 21 are protected by the 44th Amendment.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Article 19 can be suspended.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Article 22 can be suspended under Art 359.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2022 Paper I - Set B Q37 (Option D)
question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding the Election Commission of India is NOT correct?
options: The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners enjoy equal powers and receive equal salaries and allowances.
In case of difference of opinion between the CEC and other Election Commissioners, the matter is decided by the Commission by majority.
An Election Commissioner can be removed from office on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
The Constitution provides that a retired Election Commissioner is completely debarred from any future appointment by the government.
explanation: Option D is NOT correct: The Constitution has NOT debarred retired Election Commissioners from any further appointment by the government. Options A, B, and C are verbatim statutory provisions under the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 43 Election Commission.
elimination_trap: CAG and UPSC Chairman are debarred from further government employment, but Election Commissioners are NOT debarred by the Constitution.

option_analysis.A: Correct statement: CEC and other ECs have equal pay and powers.
option_analysis.B: Correct statement: Decisions taken by majority.
option_analysis.C: Correct statement: Protected by proviso to Art 324(5).
option_analysis.D: Incorrect statement (hence correct answer): The Constitution is silent on future appointment.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2021 General Knowledge - Set C Q90 (Option A)
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the ordinance-making power of the Governor of a State under Article 213:
1. The Governor can promulgate an ordinance only when the Legislative Assembly (or both Houses where there is a Legislative Council) is not in session.
2. An ordinance promulgated by the Governor ceases to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of the state legislature.
3. The Governor can withdraw an ordinance only with the prior approval of the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 only
1, 2 and 3
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Article 213 provides that Governor can issue ordinances only during legislative recess. It lapses 6 weeks after reassembly. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Governor can withdraw an ordinance promulgated by him at any time on the advice of the Council of Ministers without requiring prior approval of the President.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 30 Governor: Legislative Powers.
elimination_trap: Statement 3 adds an unconstitutional restriction; Governor withdraws ordinance on Chief Minister advice.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are true.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.
option_analysis.C: Incomplete: Statement 2 is also correct.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2021 Paper I - Set A Q64 (Option C)
question_text: To whom does the Comptroller and Auditor General of India submit audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union?
options: The Prime Minister of India
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The President of India
The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee
explanation: Option C is correct: Under Article 151(1) of the Constitution, the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to the President, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 49 Comptroller and Auditor General.
elimination_trap: Aspirants often confuse PAC with the submission channel. CAG submits reports to President, who lays them before Parliament, where PAC examines them.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Not submitted to executive head.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Not submitted directly to Speaker.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Article 151(1) mandates submission to President of India.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: PAC examines after laying in Parliament.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Open Market Operations & Monetary Policy Transmission
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2024 General Knowledge - Set B Q55 (Option A)
question_text: When the Reserve Bank of India conducts Open Market Sales of Government Securities in the secondary market, which one of the following consequences is most likely to follow?
options: Contraction of liquidity in the banking system and an upward pressure on short-term interest rates
Expansion of money supply in the economy leading to depreciation of government bond yields
Direct increase in the fiscal deficit of the Central Government
Automatic reduction in the statutory Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) of commercial banks
explanation: Option A is correct: When the RBI sells government securities, commercial banks and investors purchase them by paying cash to the RBI. This absorbs and contracts liquidity from the commercial banking system, reducing the supply of loanable funds and exerting upward pressure on short-term interest rates.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Macroeconomics, Chapter 3 Money and Banking; Ramesh Singh Indian Economy.
elimination_trap: Selling securities absorbs money; buying securities injects money. Do not reverse the cash flow direction.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Sale absorbs cash from banks, tightening liquidity and increasing interest rates.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: It causes contraction, not expansion.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: OMO is a monetary operation, not fiscal deficit creation.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: CRR is a separate statutory instrument.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Balance of Payments (BoP) & Capital Account Convertibility
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2024 Paper I - Set C Q72 (Option B)
question_text:
With reference to the Balance of Payments (BoP) in India, which of the following are included in the "Capital Account"?
1. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)
2. External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs)
3. Remittances by Non-Resident Indians to family members
4. Special Drawing Rights (SDR) allocations by the IMF

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
explanation: Statements 1, 2, and 4 are in the Capital Account. Statement 3 (Remittances) is an unrequited transfer payment and is classified under Invisibles in the CURRENT Account. FDI, ECBs, FPI, NRI bank deposits, and SDR allocations create financial asset/liability claims and belong to the Capital Account.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Macroeconomics, Chapter 6 Open Economy Macroeconomics; RBI BoP Manual.
elimination_trap: Remittances are unilateral transfers (Current Account), whereas NRI foreign currency deposits are liabilities (Capital Account).

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Item 3 belongs to Current Account.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Items 1, 2, and 4 are pure Capital Account flows.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Item 3 fails.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Item 3 included.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) vs Reverse Repo
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2023 General Knowledge - Set A Q38 (Option C)
question_text: In the context of the Reserve Bank of India's revised liquidity management framework, what is the primary operational difference between the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) and the traditional Fixed Reverse Repo rate?
options: SDF requires collateral of Government Securities, whereas Reverse Repo is completely collateral-free.
SDF is accessible only to Primary Dealers, whereas Reverse Repo is open to all Commercial Banks.
SDF allows RBI to absorb overnight liquidity from banks without providing collateral of government securities.
SDF is an unsterilized intervention that directly alters the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR).
explanation: Option C is correct: Under Section 17 of the RBI Act (amended in 2018 and operationalized in April 2022), the SDF empowers the RBI to absorb excess overnight liquidity from commercial banks without the requirement of providing collateral of government securities, thereby overcoming the collateral constraint of traditional Reverse Repo.
standard_book_ref: RBI Monetary Policy Report; Indian Economy by Vivek Singh / Nitin Singhania.
elimination_trap: Option A presents an inverted trap: it is SDF that is collateral-free, not Reverse Repo.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Inverted fact.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: SDF is available to all LAF eligible participants.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Key innovation is non-requirement of collateral.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: It does not alter SLR.

subject: Economy
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2023 Paper I - Set B Q82 (Option D)
question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in India is NOT correct?
options: It consists of six members: three from RBI and three appointed by the Central Government.
The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India is the ex-officio Chairperson of the MPC.
Each member of the MPC has one vote, and in the event of an equality of votes, the Governor has a second or casting vote.
The members appointed by the Central Government hold office for a period of five years and are eligible for re-appointment.
explanation: Option D is NOT correct: Under Section 45ZB of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the external members appointed by the Central Government hold office for a period of FOUR years (not five) and are NOT eligible for re-appointment. Options A, B, and C are accurate statutory provisions.
standard_book_ref: RBI Act 1934, Section 45ZB; Ramesh Singh Indian Economy.
elimination_trap: Tenure is 4 years and re-appointment is explicitly barred to maintain independence.

option_analysis.A: Correct statement: 6 members (3 internal + 3 external).
option_analysis.B: Correct statement: RBI Governor is Chairperson.
option_analysis.C: Correct statement: Governor has casting vote under Sec 45ZL.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect statement (hence correct answer): 4-year tenure with no re-appointment.

subject: Economy
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2022 General Knowledge - Set D Q28 (Option B)
question_text: What is the fundamental difference between 'Headline Inflation' and 'Core Inflation' in an economy?
options: Headline inflation measures wholesale prices, while core inflation measures retail consumer prices.
Core inflation strips out volatile components like food and energy commodities from headline inflation.
Headline inflation is calculated by RBI, while core inflation is published by NITI Aayog.
Core inflation includes only imported manufacturing goods, while headline inflation includes domestic services.
explanation: Option B is correct: Core inflation excludes items that face volatile price movements, notably food and fuel/energy articles, to gauge the underlying long-term trend in general price level. In India, Headline CPI is the official inflation target (4% +/- 2%).
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI Indian Economic Development; Economic Survey Inflation Chapter.
elimination_trap: Both headline and core inflation can be measured from the Consumer Price Index (CPI-Combined) basket.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Both are derived from CPI retail index.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Core excludes volatile food and energy.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: NSO publishes both data sets.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Inaccurate classification.

subject: Environment & Ecology
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2024 General Knowledge - Set D Q19 (Option C)
question_text:
Which of the following wetlands in India are currently listed in the Montreux Record under the Ramsar Convention?
1. Keoladeo National Park, Rajasthan
2. Loktak Lake, Manipur
3. Chilika Lake, Odisha

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: 1 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
explanation: Option C is correct (1 and 2 only): Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) and Loktak Lake (Manipur) are the only two Indian wetlands currently maintained in the Montreux Record. Chilika Lake was placed on the Montreux Record in 1993 but was successfully removed in 2002 due to successful ecological restoration by the Chilika Development Authority.
standard_book_ref: PMF IAS Environment (Wetlands Chapter); Shankar IAS Environment.
elimination_trap: Chilika Lake was removed from Montreux Record in 2002 and won the Ramsar Wetland Conservation Award.

option_analysis.A: Incomplete: Loktak Lake is also currently in the Record.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Chilika is no longer in Montreux Record.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Only Keoladeo and Loktak remain on the list.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Chilika was removed in 2002.

subject: Environment & Ecology
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2024 Paper I - Set B Q44 (Option A)
question_text: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022, how has the structure of schedules been reformed in India?
options: The number of schedules was rationalized and reduced from six to four, including a dedicated schedule for CITES specimens.
Schedules were completely replaced by the Red List categories of the IUCN.
Vermin animals are permanently listed under a separate non-amendable Schedule V.
Plant species were excluded from statutory protection and shifted to the Forest Conservation Act.
explanation: Option A is correct: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 drastically restructured the 1972 Act by reducing 6 schedules to 4: Schedule I (highest protection for animals), Schedule II (lesser protection), Schedule III (protected plant species), and Schedule IV (specimens listed under the CITES Appendices). The vermin schedule was repealed.
standard_book_ref: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) Act Gazette; PMF IAS Environment.
elimination_trap: Vermin schedule was NOT preserved; it was eliminated, giving Central Government executive power to declare vermin by notification.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Rationalized to 4 schedules with dedicated CITES schedule.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: IUCN categories were not adopted as statutory schedules.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Schedule V was repealed.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Plants remain under statutory Schedule III.

subject: Environment & Ecology
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2023 General Knowledge - Set A Q110 (Option B)
question_text: What happens to the Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) and Dissolved Oxygen (DO) levels in an aquatic ecosystem undergoing severe cultural eutrophication caused by agricultural runoff?
options: Both BOD and DO levels increase exponentially.
BOD increases significantly, while Dissolved Oxygen (DO) levels drop precipitously.
BOD drops to zero, while Dissolved Oxygen reaches super-saturation.
Both BOD and DO remain unchanged because aquatic plants release excess oxygen.
explanation: Option B is correct: Eutrophication introduces excess nitrogen and phosphorus, triggering an algal bloom. When the dense algae die, aerobic decomposers multiply rapidly and consume dissolved oxygen to decompose organic matter. This causes Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) to spike and Dissolved Oxygen (DO) to collapse, creating hypoxic dead zones.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Biology, Chapter 16 Environmental Issues; PMF IAS Environment.
elimination_trap: High BOD means dirty water with low dissolved oxygen. High BOD and high DO never coexist in eutrophic waters.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: DO collapses as decomposers use it up.
option_analysis.B: Correct: High organic load leads to high BOD and depleted DO.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Inverse of scientific reality.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Severe shifts occur.

subject: Environment & Ecology
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2023 Paper I - Set C Q51 (Option D)
question_text: The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol aims to achieve which of the following global environmental targets?
options: Phase out mercury emissions from artisanal gold mining
Eliminate transboundary movements of hazardous electronic wastes
Ban single-use plastics across marine coastal economic zones
Phase down the production and consumption of Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)
explanation: Option D is correct: The Kigali Amendment entered into force in 2019 to phase down Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) by over 80% over the next 30 years. Although HFCs do not deplete stratospheric ozone (unlike CFCs and HCFCs), they are potent greenhouse gases with Global Warming Potentials thousands of times higher than CO2.
standard_book_ref: UNEP Montreal Protocol Secretariat; PMF IAS Climate Conventions.
elimination_trap: HFCs are non-ozone-depleting greenhouse gases. Many assume Montreal Protocol only deals with ozone depletion.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Minamata Convention deals with mercury.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Basel Convention deals with hazardous wastes.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Covered under UNEP plastic treaty negotiations.
option_analysis.D: Correct: Kigali specifically regulates HFC phase-down.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Wood's Despatch of 1854 & Colonial Educational Reforms
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2024 General Knowledge - Set C Q88 (Option C)
question_text:
Regarding the Wood's Despatch of 1854, often hailed as the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India', which of the following statements are correct?
1. It repudiated the "downward filtration theory" for mass education.
2. It recommended English as the sole medium of instruction at both primary and higher education levels.
3. It recommended a system of grants-in-aid to encourage private enterprise in education.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Wood's Despatch repudiated the downward filtration theory and urged the government to assume responsibility for mass education. It emphasized vernacular languages for primary school education, while English was advocated for higher university education. Statement 2 is incorrect because it did not mandate English as the sole medium at primary level. Statement 3 is correct: it established grants-in-aid for private schools.
standard_book_ref: Spectrum A Brief History of Modern India, Chapter on Development of Education under British Rule.
elimination_trap: Statement 2 uses the extreme word "sole medium at both primary and higher levels". Wood's Despatch strongly supported vernacular at primary levels.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Statement 2 is historically false.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Statement 2 is false.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Statements 1 and 3 are accurate.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Contains statement 2.

subject: History & Culture
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2024 Paper I - Set D Q91 (Option B)
question_text: Which of the following Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka provides a vivid autobiographical description of the tragedy of the Kalinga War and announces the victory of 'Dhamma-vijaya' (conquest by righteousness) over military conquest?
options: Major Rock Edict X
Major Rock Edict XIII
Major Rock Edict VII
Major Rock Edict II
explanation: Option B is correct: Major Rock Edict XIII is the famous edict recounting Ashoka's conquest of Kalinga in his 8th regnal year (c. 261 BCE), expressing deep remorse over the slaughter, death, and deportation of 150,000 people, and declaring that conquest by Dhamma is the only true victory.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History Part I; Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India.
elimination_trap: Rock Edict II deals with medical treatment for humans and animals; Rock Edict XIII deals with Kalinga war and Hellenistic kings.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Edict X denounces individual desire for fame and glory.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Major Rock Edict XIII contains the Kalinga narrative and names five Greek kings.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Edict VII calls for religious tolerance across all sects.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Edict II deals with social welfare and botanical gardens.

subject: History & Culture
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2023 General Knowledge - Set B Q77 (Option A)
question_text: In the Vijayanagara Empire, the terms 'Amara-nayakas' and 'Amaram' referred to which one of the following institutional arrangements?
options: Military commanders who were given territories (amaram) to govern and maintain troops for the Raya
Hereditary revenue collectors who paid annual tribute directly to provincial governors
Guild masters of international trade operating across the Coromandel coast
Chief priests responsible for the administration of temple devadana lands
explanation: Option A is correct: As documented by Portuguese chroniclers Fernao Nuniz and Domingo Paes, the amara-nayaka system was a major political innovation of the Vijayanagara Empire (similar to the Iqta system of Delhi Sultanate). Amara-nayakas were military commanders who were granted territories (amaram) to collect taxes, maintain contingents of foot-soldiers and horses for the King (Raya), and send an annual tribute.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History Part II, Chapter 7 An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara.
elimination_trap: They were not merely revenue collectors or guild masters; they were armed military governors holding contingent quotas.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Military chiefs given amaram territories for revenue and force maintenance.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Amara-nayakas were military lords, not ordinary revenue officials.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Guilds were chettis/kudirai chettis.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Temple managers were sthanikas.

subject: History & Culture
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2022 Paper I - Set A Q105 (Option D)
question_text: Which one of the following demands put forward by Mahatma Gandhi was firmly REJECTED by Viceroy Lord Irwin during the negotiations of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931)?
options: Immediate release of all political prisoners not convicted of violence
Remission of all fines not yet collected by the colonial government
Right to make salt for domestic consumption along coastal villages
A public inquiry into police excesses and commutation of death sentences of Bhagat Singh and comrades
explanation: Option D is correct: Viceroy Irwin accepted the release of non-violent political prisoners, return of confiscated lands, and right to make salt along the coast. However, Irwin categorically rejected two demands: (1) A public judicial inquiry into police excesses, and (2) Commutation of the death sentence of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru to life imprisonment.
standard_book_ref: Spectrum A Brief History of Modern India, Chapter on Civil Disobedience Movement.
elimination_trap: Irwin refused to demoralize the police force by conceding an inquiry into police brutalities.

option_analysis.A: Accepted by Irwin.
option_analysis.B: Accepted by Irwin.
option_analysis.C: Accepted by Irwin.
option_analysis.D: Firmly rejected by Irwin (hence correct answer).

subject: Geography
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2024 General Knowledge - Set A Q63 (Option D)
question_text: Which of the following atmospheric mechanisms is primarily responsible for steering the extra-tropical winter cyclonic depressions (Western Disturbances) into Northern India?
options: The Tropical Easterly Jet Stream blowing over peninsular India
The South-West Monsoon Somali low-level jet
The Northeast trade winds blowing across the Bay of Bengal
The Sub-Tropical Westerly Jet Stream flowing south of the Himalayas
explanation: Option D is correct: During winter, the Sub-Tropical Westerly Jet Stream is bifurcated by the Tibetan Plateau. Its southern branch blows eastward south of the Himalayas at about 9-12 km altitude and steers mid-latitude cyclonic storms originating over the Mediterranean Sea and Caspian Sea across Iran and Pakistan into Northern India as Western Disturbances.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Chapter 4 Climate; D.R. Khullar Geography.
elimination_trap: Tropical Easterly Jet occurs in summer, not winter. Somali Jet drives the SW monsoon.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Easterly Jet is an upper tropospheric summer feature.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Somali jet is a summer low-level feature.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Surface trade winds do not steer upper mid-latitude cyclones.
option_analysis.D: Correct: Southern branch of Sub-Tropical Westerly Jet Stream.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Submarine Relief: Continental Shelves vs Trenches
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2024 Paper I - Set A Q52 (Option A)
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the Continental Shelf of oceans:
1. Continental shelves are shallow sea zones with a gentle average slope of 1° or even less.
2. The Siberian Shelf in the Arctic Ocean is the largest continental shelf in the world.
3. The continental shelves are completely devoid of marine life and mineral resources due to wave erosion.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Continental shelves have an average gradient of 1° or less and average depth of 120-200 meters. The Siberian shelf in the Arctic Ocean stretches over 1,500 km in width and is the widest on Earth. Statement 3 is completely false: continental shelves receive abundant sunlight (photic zone), making them the richest fishing grounds on Earth (e.g. Grand Banks) and massive reservoirs of offshore petroleum and natural gas (e.g. Bombay High, Persian Gulf).
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Chapter 13 Water (Oceans).
elimination_trap: Extreme statement 3: "completely devoid of marine life and mineral resources" is absurd since most fisheries and offshore oil come from continental shelves.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are geomorphological facts.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Indian Drainage: Superimposed vs Antecedent Rivers
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2023 General Knowledge - Set D Q99 (Option C)
question_text: Which one of the following rivers is an example of an 'Antecedent Drainage' system that cut deep gorges through the rising Himalayas?
options: Gomti
Yamuna
Indus
Betwa
explanation: Option C is correct: Antecedent rivers are older than the mountains through which they flow. As the Himalayas were uplifted during the Tertiary period, rivers like the Indus, Sutlej, and Brahmaputra maintained their courses by cutting deep V-shaped gorges through the rising ranges (e.g., the Indus gorge at Bunji in Kashmir, over 5,000 meters deep).
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3 Drainage System.
elimination_trap: Gomti originates from Fulhar Jheel in the plains; Betwa is a peninsular river flowing into Yamuna. Only Indus/Sutlej/Brahmaputra are classic antecedent rivers.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Gomti is a plain river.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Yamuna originates from Yamunotri glacier on the southern slopes.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Indus cuts through Ladakh and Zanskar ranges via antecedent incision.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Betwa is a peninsular Vindhyan river.

subject: Science & Technology
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2024 General Knowledge - Set B Q102 (Option B)
question_text:
Total Internal Reflection (TIR) occurs when light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle. Which of the following phenomena are based on Total Internal Reflection?
1. Propagation of light through an optical fibre cable
2. Mirage formation in hot deserts
3. Twinkling of stars in the night sky
4. Sparkle of a cut diamond

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
explanation: Option B is correct (1, 2, and 4 only): Optical fibres, desert mirages, and the brilliance of diamonds operate on Total Internal Reflection. In contrast, the twinkling of stars is caused by atmospheric refraction through layers of air of varying optical densities, not by Total Internal Reflection.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class X Science, Chapter 10 Light: Reflection and Refraction; Class XII Physics Optics.
elimination_trap: Twinkling of stars is always atmospheric refraction, a favorite UPSC distinction.

option_analysis.A: Incomplete: Diamond sparkle (critical angle ~24.4°) is also based on TIR.
option_analysis.B: Correct: 1, 2, and 4 are based on TIR; 3 is atmospheric refraction.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Optical fibres (1) are the quintessential engineering application of TIR.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Includes item 3.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Biotechnology: mRNA Vaccines vs Conventional Vaccines
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2024 Paper I - Set A Q85 (Option A)
question_text: In the context of modern vaccine technologies, what is the key distinction of mRNA vaccines (such as those developed for COVID-19) compared to traditional attenuated or inactivated viral vaccines?
options: mRNA vaccines introduce synthetic genetic instructions encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles to direct host cells to produce the harmless spike protein antigens.
mRNA vaccines enter the cell nucleus and permanently integrate into the human host genome via reverse transcriptase.
mRNA vaccines contain live weakened viral pathogens that replicate in the blood to trigger natural immunity.
mRNA vaccines provide passive ready-made monoclonal antibodies that bypass the host's adaptive immune response.
explanation: Option A is correct: mRNA vaccines deliver messenger RNA encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles into the cytoplasm of host cells. The cell's ribosomes translate this code into the viral spike protein, prompting the immune system to produce antibodies and T-cell responses. mRNA never enters the nucleus and does not integrate into host DNA. It degrades naturally within hours.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Biology, Chapter 8 Human Health and Disease; WHO Vaccine Guidelines.
elimination_trap: Myth trap: mRNA NEVER alters or integrates into human genomic DNA; it operates strictly in the cytoplasm.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Delivers mRNA template in lipid nanoparticles for cytosolic translation.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: mRNA cannot enter nucleus or alter DNA.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: That describes live-attenuated vaccines.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: That describes passive antibody therapy, not active vaccination.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Space Exploration: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2023 General Knowledge - Set C Q47 (Option B)
question_text: At which of the following locations is NASA/ESA/CSA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) positioned to observe the early universe?
options: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) at 550 km altitude alongside the Hubble Space Telescope
The Second Sun-Earth Lagrange Point (L2), approximately 1.5 million kilometers away from Earth
The First Sun-Earth Lagrange Point (L1), directly facing the Sun
A geosynchronous transfer orbit positioned over the North Pole
explanation: Option B is correct: JWST is stationed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (L2), located approximately 1.5 million km from Earth in the anti-sunward direction. This enables its sunshield to permanently block light and heat from the Sun, Earth, and Moon, keeping its infrared sensors cooled to near absolute zero (-233°C).
standard_book_ref: ISRO / NASA Science Briefs; Science & Technology by Ravi P. Agrahari.
elimination_trap: L1 is where solar observation satellites like SOHO and India's Aditya-L1 are placed; JWST is at L2 looking into deep space.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Hubble is in LEO; JWST is 1.5 million km away.
option_analysis.B: Correct: L2 Lagrange Point.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: L1 is for solar observatories (Aditya-L1).
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Not a geosynchronous orbit.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2020 General Knowledge - Set A Q11 (Option B)
question_text:
Which among the following terms were added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: 1 and 2 only

2 and 4 only
explanation: Option B is correct: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added three new words to the Preamble—Socialist, Secular, and Integrity. "Republic" was already part of the original Preamble adopted on 26th November 1949.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 4 Preamble of the Constitution.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2020 Paper I - Set B Q53 (Option C)
question_text: Which one of the following is NOT classified under the Gandhian principles of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India?
options: To organize village panchayats and endow them with necessary powers (Article 40)
To promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operation basis in rural areas (Article 43)
To secure for all citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India (Article 44)
To prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs which are injurious to health (Article 47)
explanation: Option C is correct: Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code) represents a Liberal-Intellectual principle, NOT a Gandhian principle. Articles 40 (Village Panchayats), 43 (Cottage industries), 43B (Cooperative societies), 46 (Educational/economic interests of SC/ST), 47 (Prohibition of intoxicants), and 48 (Prohibition of slaughter of cows/calves) represent Gandhian principles.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 8 Directive Principles of State Policy.

option_analysis.B: Gandhian principle.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Parliamentary Motions: Adjournment vs Calling Attention
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2019 General Knowledge - Set C Q76 (Option A)
question_text:
With reference to parliamentary proceedings in the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements regarding an 'Adjournment Motion':
1. It requires the support of at least 50 members to be admitted.
2. It introduces an element of censure against the government.
3. Rajya Sabha has equal power to move an Adjournment Motion.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. An Adjournment Motion draws attention of the House to a definite matter of urgent public importance and needs support of 50 members. Because it interrupts normal business and carries an element of censure, it is permitted ONLY in the Lok Sabha. Rajya Sabha is not permitted to make use of this device (Statement 3 is false).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 22 Parliament: Motions.
elimination_trap: Rajya Sabha cannot move an Adjournment Motion or a No-Confidence Motion.

option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.

upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2021 General Knowledge - Set D Q61 (Option D)
question_text: Under the Reserve Bank of India's revised Priority Sector Lending (PSL) norms, what is the total mandatory PSL target for Domestic Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding RRBs and Small Finance Banks)?
options: 18 percent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)
25 percent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)
30 percent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)
40 percent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)
explanation: Option D is correct: Domestic Scheduled Commercial Banks and Foreign Banks with 20 branches and above are mandated to allocate 40% of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or Credit Equivalent Amount of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE) to the priority sector (18% for Agriculture, 10% for Micro Enterprises, and 12% for Weaker Sections).
standard_book_ref: RBI Priority Sector Lending Guidelines Master Direction; Ramesh Singh Indian Economy.

subject: Economy
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2020 Paper I - Set A Q88 (Option B)
question_text: In public finance in India, 'Fiscal Deficit' is equal to which one of the following expressions?
options: Total Expenditure - Total Receipts
Total Expenditure - (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts)
Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts
Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments
explanation: Option B is correct: Fiscal Deficit represents the total borrowing requirements of the government from all sources: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure - (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts such as recovery of loans and disinvestment proceeds). Option A equals zero in budget accounting; Option C is Revenue Deficit; Option D is Primary Deficit.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Macroeconomics, Chapter 5 Government Budget and the Economy.
elimination_trap: Debt-creating capital receipts (borrowings) are excluded from receipts to compute the deficit.

option_analysis.C: Incorrect: That defines Revenue Deficit.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: That defines Primary Deficit.

question_text: At which of the following Harappan sites was a massive tidal dockyard connected to the Gulf of Khambhat discovered by archaeologist S.R. Rao?

Dholavira
Lothal
Banawali

Birsa and Komaram Bheem
Alluri Sitarama Raju and Gam Mallu Dora
Titu Mir and Haji Shariatullah

option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Birsa Munda was in 1899; Komaram Bheem in Telangana.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Classification of Clouds: Cirrus, Cumulonimbus, Stratus
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2022 General Knowledge - Set A Q82 (Option D)
question_text: Which of the following types of clouds are high-altitude (8,000–12,000 m), thin and detached, having a feathery appearance, and composed entirely of ice crystals?
options: Cumulonimbus clouds
Stratus clouds
Altocumulus clouds
Cirrus clouds
explanation: Option D is correct: Cirrus clouds are formed at high altitudes (8,000–12,000 m). They are thin, wispy, and detached with a feather-like appearance, white in colour, and formed entirely of microscopic ice crystals due to sub-zero temperatures. Cumulonimbus are towering vertical storm clouds; Stratus are layered low clouds.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Chapter 11 Water in the Atmosphere.
elimination_trap: Cumulonimbus produce severe thunderstorms, but Cirrus are fair-weather ice-crystal clouds.

option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Low layered clouds.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Medium clouds (2,000-6,000m).
option_analysis.D: Correct: High feather-like ice crystal clouds.

subject: Geography
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2022 Paper I - Set C Q34 (Option B)
question_text: Laterite soils in India develop primarily under which of the following climatic and pedogenic conditions?
options: Arid conditions with intense wind abrasion and salt encrustation
Tropical regions with high temperature and alternating wet and dry seasons with intense leaching
Sub-polar tundra conditions with permafrost and waterlogged peat
Semi-arid alluvial floodplains subject to seasonal inundation
explanation: Option B is correct: Laterite soils (from Latin "later" meaning brick) develop in areas with high temperature and heavy seasonal rainfall. Intense leaching by heavy rain washes away silica and lime, leaving behind an infertile residual soil rich in iron oxide and aluminum hydroxide compounds. Found in Western Ghats, Odisha, and parts of Assam.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Chapter 6 Soils.
elimination_trap: Laterite is formed by intense chemical LEACHING (desilication), not by arid evaporation.

option_analysis.B: Correct: Tropical wet and dry climate with intense leaching.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: That describes tundra soils.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: That describes alluvial khadar soils.

sub_topic: Cell Biology: Mitochondria and Chloroplast Semiautonomy

question_text: Mitochondria and Chloroplasts are regarded as semi-autonomous cell organelles because they contain which of the following cellular components?
options: Golgi bodies and endoplasmic reticulum
Cell wall and central vacuole
Their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes
Lysosomal hydrolytic enzymes and centrosomes
explanation: Option C is correct: According to the Endosymbiotic Theory, mitochondria and chloroplasts originated as symbiotic prokaryotic organisms engulfed by ancestral eukaryotic cells. Consequently, they possess their own circular double-stranded DNA and their own 70S ribosomes, allowing them to synthesize some of their own structural proteins and replicate independently by fission.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 8 Cell: The Unit of Life.

subject: Polity & Governance
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2025 General Knowledge - Set A Q28 (Option B)
question_text:
In the context of the legislative powers of the Governor under Article 200 of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Governor can withhold assent to a Bill passed by the State Legislature indefinitely without returning it.
2. When a Bill is returned by the Governor with a message for reconsideration, the Legislature must reconsider it within six months.
3. If the Bill is passed again by the Legislature with or without amendment, the Governor cannot withhold assent therefrom.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: As clarified by the Supreme Court of India in State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to the Governor (2023), the phrase "as soon as possible" in the first proviso to Article 200 implies that the Governor cannot sit on a bill indefinitely or pocket-veto it without either granting assent, withholding assent and returning it with a message, or reserving it for the President. Statement 2 is correct (6 months reconsideration window). Statement 3 is correct: the Governor has no pocket veto after re-passage.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity (7th Ed.), Chapter 30 Governor: Assent to Bills; Article 200 Bare Act.
elimination_trap: Statement 1 assumes Governor has unlimited pocket veto; Supreme Court held Governor must act "as soon as possible".

option_analysis.B: Correct: Statements 2 and 3 are accurate constitutional provisions.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Statement 1 is false.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Contains statement 1.

subject: Economy

60 percent of the highest basic pay drawn during the entire service career
A variable corpus-linked annuity with no guaranteed minimum floor
40 percent of the last drawn gross salary including Dearness Allowance

standard_book_ref: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Notification; Economic Survey Public Finance.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Abolition of Angel Tax & Venture Capital in India
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2025 Paper I - Set A Q67 (Option D)
question_text: The Union Budget 2024–25 announced the complete abolition of the 'Angel Tax' under Section 56(2)(viib) of the Income Tax Act. What was the original operational mechanism of this tax?

A capital gains tax on angel investors who sell shares within six months of startup incorporation
A customs tariff on import of deep-tech high-performance computing hardware
Taxation of capital raised by unlisted startups from investors in excess of the Fair Market Value (FMV) as income from other sources

subject: Environment & Ecology
sub_topic: Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA) & Clean Energy Transition
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2025 General Knowledge - Set D Q94 (Option B)

India, Brazil and the United States
India, Saudi Arabia and Russia
India, Australia and France

option_analysis.D: Incorrect.

subject: Geography
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2025 Paper I - Set C Q41 (Option C)
question_text: In 2024, the United Kingdom agreed to cede sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago to which Indian Ocean nation, while retaining the joint UK-US military base on Diego Garcia?
options: Seychelles
Maldives
Mauritius
Madagascar
explanation: Option C is correct: In a historic treaty agreed in October 2024 following advisory opinions of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and UN General Assembly resolutions, the UK recognized the sovereignty of Mauritius over the Chagos Archipelago in the Indian Ocean, while securing a 99-year lease for the strategically vital joint UK-US military facility on the atoll of Diego Garcia.
standard_book_ref: Oxford World Atlas; International Relations MEA Annual Report.
elimination_trap: Chagos was historically separated from Mauritius before Mauritian independence in 1968, making Mauritius the sovereign claimant.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Seychelles lies west.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Maldives is north of Chagos.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Mauritius.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Madagascar lies in Mozambique Channel.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Aditya-L1 Mission: Halo Orbit Insertion & Payloads
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2025 General Knowledge - Set B Q81 (Option A)
question_text: In January 2024, ISRO successfully inserted its solar observatory spacecraft Aditya-L1 into a halo orbit around which gravitational equilibrium point in the Sun-Earth system?
options: First Sun-Earth Lagrange Point (L1), located approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth towards the Sun
Second Sun-Earth Lagrange Point (L2), located 1.5 million kilometers away from Earth in the anti-sunward direction
Third Sun-Earth Lagrange Point (L3), located directly on the opposite side of the Sun
Fourth Sun-Earth Lagrange Point (L4), trailing Earth in its orbit by 60 degrees
explanation: Option A is correct: Aditya-L1 is placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point, approximately 1.5 million km from Earth. L1 provides an uninterrupted, continuous view of the Sun without any occultation or eclipses, enabling its 7 scientific payloads (including VELC, SUIT, and ASPEX) to observe solar coronal mass ejections and space weather in real time.
standard_book_ref: ISRO Aditya-L1 Mission Dossier; Science & Technology by Ravi P. Agrahari.
elimination_trap: L2 is where deep-space observatories like JWST are placed to look away from the Sun; L1 is where solar observatories look towards the Sun.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange Point.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: L2 is for JWST / deep-space telescopes.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: L3 is on the opposite side behind the Sun.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: L4 is a Trojan point.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) & Decolonized Criminal Jurisprudence
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2026 General Knowledge - Set A Q19 (Option C)
question_text: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced the colonial Indian Penal Code, 1860), which of the following represents a novel statutory punishment introduced for petty offences?
options: Rigorous imprisonment in military barracks
Civil forfeiture of ancestral agricultural land
Community Service as a formal penal punishment
Mandatory loss of citizenship rights for five years
explanation: Option C is correct: For the first time in Indian statutory criminal jurisprudence, "Community Service" was formally codified as one of the categories of punishment under Section 4 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. It can be awarded for minor offences like petty theft, public defamation, and misconduct by an intoxicated person to promote restorative justice.
standard_book_ref: Ministry of Home Affairs BNS Handbook; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity (7th Ed.) Appendix.
elimination_trap: Community service was previously used informally by judges under probation laws, but BNS made it an explicit statutory punishment category under penal law.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Community service codified under Section 4 BNS.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Citizenship deprivation cannot be imposed under penal code.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 & Article 262
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2026 Paper I - Set D Q33 (Option B)
question_text: Under Article 262 of the Constitution of India and the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, which of the following statements regarding the jurisdiction of courts is correct?
options: The Supreme Court has original and exclusive jurisdiction under Article 131 to decide inter-state river water disputes directly.
Neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction in respect of any water dispute referred to an Inter-State Water Dispute Tribunal.
A decision of the Water Disputes Tribunal can be appealed as a statutory right before a five-judge Constitution Bench of the High Court.
The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has superseding jurisdiction over all Inter-State Water Dispute Tribunals.
explanation: Option B is correct: Article 262(2) empowers Parliament to enact legislation barring the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and all other courts in respect of the adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-state rivers. Section 11 of the 1956 Act explicitly bars the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts once a dispute is referred to a Tribunal (though Special Leave Petitions under Article 136 on questions of law/fundamental rights can still be heard by the Supreme Court).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 15 Inter-State Relations: River Water Disputes.
elimination_trap: Article 131 original jurisdiction excludes inter-state river disputes when Parliament enacts an exclusion law under Article 262.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Art 131 jurisdiction is barred by Art 262.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Article 262(2) and Section 11 bar jurisdiction of courts.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: High Courts have zero appellate jurisdiction.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: NGT cannot adjudicate inter-state water sharing.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework for NBFCs
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (II) 2026 General Knowledge - Set A Q60 (Option A)
question_text: Under the Reserve Bank of India's Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework extended to Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), which of the following three financial parameters serve as the primary monitoring triggers?
options: Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR), Net Non-Performing Assets (NNPA), and Tier 1 Leverage Ratio
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), and Fiscal Deficit
Market Capitalization, Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) quota, and Net Profit Margin
Current Account Deficit, Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR), and Core Inflation
explanation: Option A is correct: RBI introduced the PCA framework for upper, middle, and deposit-taking NBFCs based on three core indicators: (1) Capital adequacy (CRAR and Tier-I capital), (2) Asset quality (Net Non-Performing Assets / NNPA ratio), and (3) Leverage (Tier-1 Leverage Ratio). Crossing risk thresholds triggers restrictions on dividend distribution, branch expansion, and capital expenditure.
standard_book_ref: RBI Master Direction - Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework for NBFCs; Ramesh Singh Indian Economy.
elimination_trap: NBFCs do NOT maintain CRR; therefore any option containing CRR or SLR is immediately eliminated.

option_analysis.A: Correct: CRAR, NNPA, and Tier-1 Leverage ratio.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: NBFCs do not maintain CRR with RBI.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: Stock market capitalization is not a regulatory PCA trigger.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Macroeconomic indicators (CAD, inflation) are not entity-level triggers.

subject: Environment & Ecology
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2026 Paper I - Set B Q77 (Option D)
question_text: Under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) adopted under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), what is the flagship '30x30' conservation target committed to by parties by 2030?
options: Ensure 30 percent reduction in global plastic waste and 30 percent reduction in carbon dioxide emissions by 2030
Phase out 30 hazardous agrochemicals and achieve 30 percent renewable energy generation in all developing countries
Cut global food waste by 30 percent and allocate 30 percent of agricultural land to organic farming
Ensure that at least 30 percent of terrestrial, inland water, and coastal and marine areas are effectively conserved and managed through protected areas and OECMs by 2030
explanation: Option D is correct: Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (known as the "30x30 Target") commits all signatory nations to ensure that by 2030, at least 30% of degraded terrestrial, inland water, and marine/coastal ecosystems are under effective restoration, and at least 30% of terrestrial and marine areas are conserved through ecologically representative, well-connected protected areas and Other Effective area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs).
standard_book_ref: UNEP Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) COP15 Decision 15/4; PMF IAS Biodiversity.
elimination_trap: 30x30 refers strictly to spatial conservation of LAND and OCEANS (30% by 2030), not emissions or plastic reductions.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Not a spatial biodiversity target.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect.
option_analysis.D: Correct: 30% of terrestrial and marine areas conserved by 2030.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Critical Minerals: Lithium Exploration in India
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2026 General Knowledge - Set C Q84 (Option C)
question_text:
In the context of India's critical and strategic minerals exploration, in which of the following regions did the Geological Survey of India (GSI) establish inferred lithium mineral resources (G3 stage)?
1. Salal-Haimana area in Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir
2. Katghora block in Korba district of Chhattisgarh
3. Kolar Gold Fields in Karnataka

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: 1 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
explanation: Option C is correct (1 and 2 only): GSI established 5.9 million tonnes of inferred lithium resources in the bauxite-clay composite in Salal-Haimana (Reasi, J&K) and subsequent lithium-rare metal blocks in Katghora (Korba district, Chhattisgarh). KGF in Karnataka is an abandoned deep underground gold mine, not a lithium reserve.
standard_book_ref: Ministry of Mines Annual Report; Geological Survey of India (GSI) Mineral Exploration Bulletins.
elimination_trap: Kolar is exclusively historic gold mining; lithium pegmatite reserves in Karnataka are in Marlagalla-Allapatna in Mandya, not KGF.

option_analysis.A: Incomplete: Katghora in Chhattisgarh is also a major lithium auction block.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: KGF has no lithium.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are authentic GSI critical mineral sites.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Includes item 3.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Temple Engineering: Kakatiya Sandbox Technology & Ramappa
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CAPF (AC) 2026 Paper I - Set B Q92 (Option A)
question_text: The 13th-century Kakatiya Ramappa Temple (Rudreshwara Temple) in Palampet, Telangana—inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site—survived massive earthquakes over eight centuries primarily due to which unique architectural and engineering technique?
options: The "Sandbox Technique" foundation filled with sand, granite powder, and jaggery to absorb seismic earthquake waves
Deep underground pneumatic caissons anchored into Himalayan tectonic faults
Monolithic basalt excavation carved into the Deccan trap cliffside without foundation joints
The use of reinforced iron cramps with Roman hydraulic pozzolana cement
explanation: Option A is correct: Ramappa temple (built in 1213 CE by Recharla Rudra during the reign of Kakatiya ruler Ganapati Deva) is engineered with a subterranean "Sandbox Technique" foundation. The foundation pit was packed with a cushion of fine sand, lime, jaggery, and karakkaya (black myrobalan), which acts as a seismic shock absorber. Additionally, its upper gopuram was built using unique floating light-weight porous bricks.
standard_book_ref: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) World Heritage Dossier; Nitin Singhania Indian Art & Culture.
elimination_trap: Sandbox foundation technology is the signature engineering miracle of Kakatiya temples.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Sandbox technique foundation.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Modern 19th-century bridge engineering.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: That describes Ellora Kailasa temple.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Roman pozzolana was not used in Deccan architecture.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Gaganyaan Mission: Crew Escape System & CE-20 Cryogenic Engine
upsc_official_key: Official Key: CDS (I) 2026 General Knowledge - Set D Q108 (Option B)
question_text: Which heavy-lift launch vehicle of ISRO has been human-rated (HLVM3) to carry the orbital module carrying Indian astronauts (Vyomnauts) into a 400 km Low Earth Orbit under the Gaganyaan programme?
options: Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle - XL (PSLV-XL)
Launch Vehicle Mark-3 (LVM3 / GSLV Mk-III)
Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV)
Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mk-II (GSLV Mk-II)
explanation: Option B is correct: ISRO human-rated the LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3, formerly GSLV Mk-III) into the HLVM3. It features human-rated solid strap-on boosters (HS200), a human-rated core liquid stage (L110), and the qualified CE-20 cryogenic upper stage (C25), along with the Crew Escape System (CES) tested in TV-D1/TV-D2 missions.
standard_book_ref: ISRO Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC) Gaganyaan Overview; Science & Technology Ravi Agrahari.
elimination_trap: PSLV lacks payload capacity for the 8-tonne Gaganyaan module; LVM3 is the designated rocket.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: PSLV is for lighter remote sensing satellites.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Human-Rated LVM3 (HLVM3).
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: SSLV is for nano/micro satellites (up to 500 kg).
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: GSLV Mk-II uses cryogenic upper stage not human-rated for Gaganyaan.
